scientific_scope.statement: For every m, the colouring col m of [22m] (evens one colour; odd k <= 8m or k > 20m a second; other odds a third) has exactly 99 m^2 + 3 m rainbow ordered Schur triples (witness_count); for every m >= 1 this exceeds (9/22) binom(22m,2) (family_above); for every n >= 3608 some 3-colouring of [n] has more than (2/5 + 1/220) binom(n,2) rainbow ordered Schur triples (everywhere_above); and as one theorem not_tightnessConjecture : not TightnessConjecture, where TightnessConjecture says: for all positive naturals p, q there is N such that for all n >= N and all c : Nat -> Fin 3, 5q * 2R(c,n) <= (2q + 5p) * n(n-1). Also not_tightnessConjectureLiminf. The count is proved equal to the length of the rainbow sublist of an explicit duplicate-free list of all Schur pairs of [n] (rainbowCount_eq_length, mem_schurPairs, nodup_schurPairs, schurPairs_length).
binding_points: The conjecture is asymptotic: one n refutes nothing; the certificate has the exact count for all m, a strict inequality at every n = 22m and a fixed margin at every n >= 3608 (lim, limsup and liminf readings all refuted)
Ordered Schur triples normalised by binom(n,2), as the source's Section 2; the count is the source's own sum of r(z), proved equal to the (x,y)-indexed count and to a list cardinality
Direction: the conjecture is an upper bound over all 3-colourings; the lower-bound half is the source's theorem and is untouched; the uniqueness half is not addressed
epsilon is rational p/q, cross-multiplied; the passage to real epsilon is a prose argument, not Lean
Maximum over colourings is expressed as a universal quantifier over c : Nat -> Fin 3; only colours of 1..n matter (rainbowCount_congr)
